definitions.explanation: Makeup applied in excessive amounts, giving an unnatural or overdone appearance. Usually carries a negative nuance.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}はいつも{厚化粧|あつげしょう}だ。
{厚化粧|あつげしょう}で{素顔|すがお}がわからない。
examples.english: The heavy makeup makes it impossible to tell what her real face looks like.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}いのに{厚化粧|あつげしょう}をすると、かえって{老|ふ}けて{見|み}えることがある。
examples.english: Even young people can look older when they wear too much makeup.

notes:
USAGE:
{厚化粧|あつげしょう} is generally negative, implying the makeup is excessive or tasteless. It is most often used about women but can describe anyone. The opposite is {薄化粧|うすげしょう} (light makeup), which has a positive nuance of natural beauty.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {厚化粧|あつげしょう}の{女性|じょせい} (a heavily made-up woman)
- {厚化粧|あつげしょう}をする (to put on heavy makeup)
- {厚化粧|あつげしょう}で{隠|かく}す (to hide behind heavy makeup)

FORMS:
{厚|あつ}い (thick) + {化粧|けしょう} (makeup). The reading changes from けしょう to げしょう in this compound (rendaku).
